title: Segmentation faults and memory corruption using ZFS git with init_on_alloc=0 init_on_free=0
body: I'm running Arch Linux with kernel 6.11.5-zen1-1-zen and OpenZFS 2.3.99.r34.g152ae5c9bc on a Dell Latitude E5470 with 32 GB of memory. With init_on_alloc=0 init_on_free=0 on the kernel command line, starting a Docker Compose project with Rails and MySQL can lead to segmentation faults; shortly afterward most commands and Plasma may crash. There is initially nothing useful in dmesg, while journalctl shows apparently random processes dumping core. OpenZFS 2.2.6 is stable for me, and the machine passes its BIOS memory test. I use several custom ZFS module options and do not use zvols.

symptoms_visible: After I start a Docker Compose project containing Rails and MySQL, processes begin receiving segmentation faults; soon afterward commands and Plasma can also crash.
The first failures leave nothing useful in dmesg, while journalctl contains core dumps from seemingly unrelated processes.
N0.label: N0 system-wide crashes reported

symptoms_visible: The crashes occur on my 32 GB Dell notebook when init_on_alloc=0 init_on_free=0 is present.
A 48 GB HP Elitedesk initially did not show the same system-wide segmentation faults with the same command-line and module options.
N1.label: N1 machine and configuration comparison

symptoms_visible: After I thought the problem had gone away and closed it as machine-specific, Docker Compose triggered the crashes again.
This time the kernel printed a warning at mm/gup.c:144 in try_grab_folio while mysqld was running.
N1_x.label: N1_x false-positive closure contradicted

symptoms_visible: Starting the MySQL container reliably produces the try_grab_folio warning and then widespread segmentation faults when the two init flags are disabled.
The same warning and crashes occur with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled set to either 0 or 1.
N2.label: N2 reproducible warning and ABD control test

symptoms_visible: With current OpenZFS master, running the shared Compose file and waiting for MySQL to initialize produces the try_grab_folio warning; afterward even simple commands such as dmesg may segfault.
On the other machine, MySQL initialization instead stops with operating-system error 12, 'Cannot allocate memory,' without the system-wide segmentation faults.
N3.label: N3 maintainer-ready MySQL reproducer

N4.label: N4 candidate change installed awaiting workload verification

symptoms_visible: With the candidate OpenZFS change installed, MySQL starts without complaints and the try_grab_folio warning and system-wide segmentation faults do not appear on the Arch, LTS, or Zen kernels I tested.
N_terminal.label: terminal candidate change verified

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on another machine with the same command-line and ZFS module options?
Does the failure follow this configuration to different hardware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the same Arch and ZFS git setup on an HP Elitedesk 800 G4 with the same command-line and module options, and it initially did not happen there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It reproduces identically on every machine I test, even without the custom kernel command-line settings.
A second Dell reproduces it, while the HP still does not.

question_patterns: On the affected notebook, does removing init_on_alloc=0 init_on_free=0 change the result?
Which command-line settings are required for the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my Dell notebook it happens only with init_on_alloc=0 init_on_free=0; without those settings it is fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes just as reliably with the default init_on_alloc and init_on_free settings.

question_patterns: How much memory is installed in each machine?
What is the memory-capacity difference between the affected and unaffected systems?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The notebook has 32 GB and the Elitedesk has 48 GB.

question_patterns: Are either of the machines at or near 100% memory usage when this occurs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Both run some Incus containers and Docker, but neither is at a hard 100% memory usage.

edges.comment: Reporter comments c5 and c7 compare the reporter's Dell notebook with the reporter's HP Elitedesk; c6 prompted the memory-capacity comparison. No other participant's setup is folded into this chain.

solution.intent: Dismiss the report as a transient, machine-specific false positive or possible hardware fault because the second machine initially did not show system-wide crashes.
solution.concrete_example: Since the other machine does not show the same crashes and the latest build currently seems fine, close this as a machine-specific false positive.

edges.comment: Reporter c7 briefly closed the issue as a false positive, but c8 immediately supplied a fresh debug-enabled reproduction with a try_grab_folio warning. The later observation falsifies the dismissal.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this with a build configured using --enable-debug and paste any kernel warning or panic it produces?
Please rerun the workload with a debug build and report the raw backtrace.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With debug enabled, I got a kernel warning at mm/gup.c:144 in try_grab_folio while mysqld was running. The trace goes through follow_page_pte, __get_user_pages, __gup_longterm_locked and get_user_pages_fast.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug build reports 'buffer modified while frozen' and never shows a try_grab_folio or get_user_pages warning.
The same try_grab_folio warning appears under a different mysqld PID.

question_patterns: Does changing zfs_abd_scatter_enabled alter the reproduction?
Please compare the workload with ABD scatter disabled and enabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first reproduced it with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled=0, then reproduced the same try_grab_folio warning with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled=1. It is unrelated to that option here.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It reproduces only when zfs_abd_scatter_enabled=0 and remains stable after setting it to 1.

edges.comment: Reporter c8-c11 ran the requested debug configuration and pasted raw kernel traces, then compared both ABD-scatter values. The user reports only the observed warning and control-test result.

question_patterns: Can you compare the result with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled set to 0 and to 1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled=0 and also with zfs_abd_scatter_enabled=1. In both cases I get the try_grab_folio warning while starting the Compose workload.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Enabling ABD scatter completely prevents the warning and crashes.

edges.comment: Recovery from the false-positive closure using reporter c9-c11. The debug warning is already known at N1_x; this edge collects the remaining module-option control test.

question_patterns: Can you verify whether the problem still occurs on current OpenZFS master?
Which exact ZFS and kernel builds produced the recent backtraces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm running current master as of today: zfs-2.3.99-90_g38c0324c0f and zfs-kmod-2.3.99-90_g38c0324c0f. All the backtraces above use that version.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Current master no longer reproduces; only an older pre-release snapshot crashes.

question_patterns: Can you share a minimal docker-compose.yml that reproduces the failure?
Please reduce the workload to something maintainers can run locally.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can't share the company application, but I can trigger it with a Compose file using mysql:8, redis:7-alpine and mailhog. The MySQL service has a named volume plus MYSQL_DATABASE=backend and MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=foo; without the environment variables it exits early and is fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it outside the private company application and cannot provide any shareable workload.
The same MySQL service reproduces without the Redis and Mailhog services.

question_patterns: What exactly happens when you run the reduced Compose file?
Which container is active when the warning appears?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Running docker compose up and waiting for MySQL initialization hits 'WARNING: CPU: 2 PID: 6555 at mm/gup.c:144 try_grab_folio+0x77/0xc0'. After that, many processes segfault and sometimes even a simple dmesg command fails.

edges.comment: Reporter c14 and c17 supplied the exact current-master version and a sanitized Compose reproducer from the reporter's own workload. Reporter c20 then volunteered the contrasting ENOMEM-only result from the reporter's other machine.

question_patterns: Can you build and install the linked candidate change so it can be tested against the same workload?
Please prepare a ZFS build from the proposed change and tell me which build you installed.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built and installed zfs-kmod-2.3.99-94_g0ffa6f3464 with the linked patch.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The proposed change does not build or load on this system, so I cannot run the workload with it.

solution.intent: Apply the maintainer's candidate OpenZFS change to the affected system so the known MySQL reproducer can be rerun against it.
solution.concrete_example: Build and install the maintainer's linked candidate change, then use the same MySQL Compose workload to determine whether the warning and crashes remain.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer's local reproduction establishes that the reporter supplied a useful OpenZFS reproducer. The linked change's implementation is not described in the issue, so its internal mechanism must not be invented.

edges.comment: Maintainer c21 reported reproducing the reporter's sanitized workload, and c25 asked the reporter to try the linked candidate change. Installing the patched ZFS package is a persistent system change, so this edge advances the system from S1 to S2 before verification.

question_patterns: Please rerun the same MySQL Compose workload on the installed candidate build and tell me what you observe.
Does MySQL start normally on the candidate build, and do the warning or system-wide crashes return?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It looks good on 6.12.1-arch1-1. MySQL starts without complaints and the problem has not appeared.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate build still produces the same try_grab_folio warning and system-wide segmentation faults.

question_patterns: Can you also rerun the workload with the installed candidate build on the LTS and Zen kernels you use?
Does the same patched build remain stable on your other kernels with init_on_alloc=0?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: 6.6.63-1-lts and 6.12.1-zen1-1 are also fine with init_on_alloc=0. Thank you so much.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Arch and Zen kernels pass, but I have not yet tested the LTS kernel.
The Arch kernel passes, but the same warning and crashes still occur on both LTS and Zen.

solution.intent: Retain the validated OpenZFS change after verifying it with the original MySQL workload, rather than dismissing the failures as hardware-specific or changing the ABD-scatter setting.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the candidate OpenZFS change installed and rerun the original MySQL Compose workload on the affected system and relevant kernels before declaring the issue resolved. The thread suspected direct I/O but did not establish the patch's internal mechanism.
solution.inference_hint: Direct I/O, zero-page behavior and HAVE_IOV_ITER_GET_PAGES2 were only maintainer hypotheses. The issue establishes the fix only at the level of the linked candidate change, followed by successful workload verification.

edges.comment: Reporter c26-c27 performed terminal-side verification after installing the candidate change: MySQL started without complaints on 6.12.1-arch1-1, and the reporter then confirmed 6.6.63-1-lts and 6.12.1-zen1-1 were also fine with init_on_alloc=0. The verification results are clarification outputs and are not prerequisites in this edge's required_info.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: a reproducible OpenZFS defect exposed while MySQL initializes in the Docker Compose workload, associated with the try_grab_folio/get_user_pages warning and corrected by the maintainer's validated change.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: current master still reproduced, the sanitized MySQL Compose workload let the maintainer reproduce it, and the candidate build was subsequently verified on the affected machine across Arch, LTS and Zen kernels.
Must not dismiss the issue as a Dell-specific false positive or hardware-memory fault; that closure was contradicted by a fresh debug reproduction and maintainer reproduction.
Must not recommend changing zfs_abd_scatter_enabled as the fix because both values reproduced the warning and crashes.
Must not state that direct I/O, the zero-page change, or HAVE_IOV_ITER_GET_PAGES2 was definitively the root cause; those remained hypotheses in the thread.

Must require verification on a build containing the candidate change before treating the issue as resolved; the reporter's successful MySQL tests on the Arch, LTS and Zen kernels provide that verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Linux and OpenZFS user who builds git packages, changes kernel command-line and module parameters, runs containers, compares kernels and machines, and can supply long kernel traces and reduced reproducers.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, candid and iterative; posts raw logs and exact versions, corrects earlier conclusions promptly, protects private company code while producing a shareable reproducer, and tests requested builds across several kernels.
